 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Croatia return to Wembley this Thursday to face England in the Nations League , looking to put last month's humiliating 7-0 defeat in Rijeka behind them. 
 The previous meeting was a difficult night for Slaven Bilic 's side, who struggled to match England's pace, intensity and physicality.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Croatia were repeatedly exposed defensively and failed to show the organisation needed to compete with their opponents.
 The result also left a lasting psychological impact. Luka Modric described the defeat as a damaging blow to the team's reputation, while Bilic admitted it was an experience that would stay with him.
 The Croatia manager has urged his players not to forget the result, hoping it will serve as motivation to avoid a repeat performance.
 A response at Wembley will not be easy. Croatia continue to rely heavily on the experience of 41-year-old Modric, while questions remain over their options in defensive midfield and out wide. They will also be without Ivan Perisic , who is suspended after picking up a second yellow card against Spain.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement For Croatia, Thursday's match is about more than the result. They need to show greater determination, defensive discipline and intensity to demonstrate that they can still compete with one of Europe's strongest sides.
